is_anopheles.evidence: The study evaluated repellents against Anopheles gambiae s.s. (Ifakara strain), Aedes aegypti, and Culex quinquefasciatus (page 11, 'Mosquito rearing').

reports_target_markers.evidence: No insecticide-resistance markers were genotyped. The paper only mentions 'knockdown resistance (Kdr)' generally in the introduction (page 2).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No molecular genotyping or resistance marker data are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: The Anopheles mosquitoes tested were from an insectary colony: 'Anopheles gambiae s.s. (Ifakara strain from Tanzania) ... reared under controlled conditions in the insectary at the International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology (icipe)' (page 11).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an original empirical research paper testing insect-derived oils as repellents.

sub_country_location.evidence: Mosquitoes used were insectary-maintained laboratory strains rather than field collections tied to specific study sites.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: No mosquito field collection dates are reported as colony strains were used.

duplicate_risk.evidence: Standard experimental study testing insectary colonies.

supplement.evidence: Supplementary files contain GC-MS volatile profiles and additional CPT data; no marker genotype data exist.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated insect-derived oils blended with plant essential oils as topical mosquito repellents against laboratory colonies of Anopheles gambiae, Aedes aegypti, and Culex quinquefasciatus using arm-in-cage trials and GC-MS VOC profiling. No insecticide-resistance marker genotyping was performed.
exclusion_reasons: Does not genotype any target insecticide-resistance markers
Does not report genotype counts or frequencies
Uses laboratory colony mosquitoes rather than African field populations
